brief.headline: The front end finally broke the wrong way for the bulls and the inventory streak stopped on the very same session: cash fell $53 to $3,219 while the three-month fell only $38 to $3,234, opening a $15 CONTANGO - the market now pays LESS for metal today than for metal in three months - and LME warrant was unchanged at 246,925 tonnes after 34 straight daily draws, so the two facts the bullish case rested on stopped supporting it in one board.
bullets: WHAT MOVED: THE PRICE FELL AND THE CURVE FELL FURTHER, WHICH IS THE ORDINARY DIRECTION BUT AN EXTRAORDINARY LEVEL. The 18-August official cash settlement is $3,219.00, down $53.00 (-1.62%), and the three-month is $3,234.00, down $38.00 (-1.16%). Because cash fell more, the spread crossed from exactly $0.00 into a $15.00 CONTANGO - the widest aluminium prompt discount on the published board since 27-February. Four sessions of monotonic decay have taken the front end from a premium to a discount. The price has now given back $154 of the $166 rally that ran from 29-July to 11-August.

WHY IT MATTERS: THE INVENTORY DRAWDOWN STOPPED ON THE SAME DAY, SO BOTH HALVES OF THE BULLISH CASE MOVED AT ONCE. LME aluminium stock was UNCHANGED at 246,925 tonnes, a reported daily change of exactly zero, ending 34 consecutive declines - confirmed independently by SMM's own flash note for the session. For seven weeks the argument was that an unbroken drawdown to a cycle low must eventually force the curve into backwardation. Instead the curve went to contango and the drawdown paused, in the same board. When two series that were supposed to confirm each other both turn together, the honest conclusion is that the underlying story was weaker than either looked alone.

THE FACT THAT REFRAMES EVERYTHING ELSE: THE INVENTORY SERIES MAY NEVER HAVE MEASURED WHAT BOTH SIDES ASSUMED. StoneX's senior metals analyst, quoted publicly on 18-August, says LME aluminium stocks outside China are 95 PER CENT RUSSIAN-ORIGIN - metal US and European buyers are prohibited from using and many Asian buyers decline to take. If that holds, the headline warrant number overstates the cushion when stock is high and overstates the scarcity when stock is falling, and a cycle-low inventory sitting next to a contango stops being a paradox at all. Separately, China's semi-finished exports hit a record 695,000 tonnes in June and it turned net exporter of aluminium alloy for the first time since 2019 - the Western shortage is being relieved by processed metal that never trades as an ingot premium.

WHAT TO WATCH: TODAY'S RING, AND WHETHER THE CONTANGO IS ONE SESSION OR A REGIME. Two specific outcomes frame it. A return to a flat or backwardated spread would mark 18-August as a one-day artefact of what was clearly a complex-wide repricing - four of the five metals moved their front ends looser, and copper's prompt premium halved on the largest single-day stock build of the cycle. A second consecutive contango, or an outright stock BUILD, would confirm that the seven-week drawdown was never about prompt scarcity. On levels: $3,159.50 is the 28-July swing low and the line below which this correction becomes deeper than a simple second wave; $3,254.60 is the 38.2% retracement of the whole 3,061.50-to-3,374 advance and the first level bulls need back.

Exchange inventory is at a cycle low of 246,925 tonnes after a seven-week drawdown, and the curve is telling you that at that inventory level the market still prefers metal in three months to metal today. An inventory series and a curve can disagree for a while; when the curve wins the argument, the honest reading is that the inventory series was measuring something other than prompt scarcity. THE 18-AUGUST NEWS FLOW SUPPLIED A CANDIDATE EXPLANATION AND IT IS SOURCED, NOT SPECULATIVE: StoneX's senior metals analyst, quoted by AL Circle on 18-August, puts LME aluminium stocks outside China at 95 per cent RUSSIAN-ORIGIN material, which physical buyers in the US and Europe are prohibited from using and many Asian buyers decline to purchase. That single fact reconciles a cycle-low inventory with a contango better than any other public explanation available today.

lme.commentary: THE 18-AUGUST RING PRINTED AND IT RESOLVED THE CONTRADICTION THAT HAS DEFINED THIS BOARD FOR A WEEK - IN THE BEARISH DIRECTION, ON BOTH LEGS AT ONCE. Cash settled $3,219.00, down $53.00 (-1.62%) on the 17-August official of $3,272.00. The three-month settled $3,234.00, down $38.00 (-1.16%). Because cash fell more than the three-month, the cash-3M spread crossed from exactly $0.00 into a $15.00 CONTANGO: the market is now paying LESS for prompt aluminium than for aluminium in three months. And on the same session the inventory series stopped: LME warrant was UNCHANGED at 246,925 tonnes, a reported change of exactly zero, ending 34 consecutive daily declines. THE PRIOR RUN PUBLISHED A SPECIFIC, FALSIFIABLE TEST AND IT IS WORTH RESTATING BEFORE SCORING IT: 'a return to backwardation would say the two-day premium was a real physical signal interrupted; a slip into contango on a 35th consecutive stock draw would be the single most bearish structural print available on this board.' Neither branch printed exactly. What printed was contango WITHOUT a 35th draw - which reaches the bearish conclusion by a shorter route, because the draw that was supposed to be the counterweight simply stopped. Scoring this honestly: the bearish branch was the closer of the two, and the dashboard's own framing understated how quickly the second series could turn. THE FIFTEEN-SESSION WINDOW NOW READS AS A COMPLETED ROUND TRIP. From $3,207.00 on 29-July the market rallied $166.00 to $3,373.00 on 11-August and has since given back $154.00 - so 93% of the advance is gone in five sessions while warrant fell another 6,475 tonnes over the same stretch. A market that surrenders almost an entire rally while its visible inventory keeps falling is not being driven by the inventory. THE READ-ACROSS FROM THE REST OF THE BOARD IS UNUSUALLY SHARP TODAY AND IT CUTS THE SAME WAY. Copper's cash fell $515.00 to $14,335.00 while its three-month fell only $235.00 to $14,080.00, collapsing the prompt premium from $535.00 to $255.00 - and copper warrant BUILT 15,725 tonnes to 223,550 tonnes, by a wide margin the largest single-day inventory build on this board in the cycle. Zinc's backwardation narrowed from $87.00 to $71.00. Nickel's contango narrowed from $210.00 to $180.00. Lead's contango widened from $46.50 to $50.50. Four of the five metals moved their front ends toward looser, and the fifth - lead - was already the loosest on the board. This was a complex-wide front-end repricing, not an aluminium-specific event, which argues against reading aluminium's contango as a verdict on aluminium's own physical balance and in favour of reading it as a repricing of prompt risk across base metals. THE SINGLE MOST USEFUL NEW PUBLIC FACT FOR INTERPRETING THE INVENTORY SERIES ARRIVED ON 18-AUGUST FROM A THIRD PARTY. StoneX's senior metals analyst, quoted by AL Circle, states that LME aluminium stocks outside China are 95 per cent RUSSIAN-ORIGIN material - metal US and European physical buyers are prohibited from using and many Asian buyers choose not to buy. If that is right, the headline warrant number has been a weak proxy for Western-accessible metal throughout this drawdown, and a cycle-low inventory sitting alongside a contango stops being a paradox. The same article frames aluminium as having 'returned to backwardation' - a framing that the 18-August board has already overtaken, and which is reported here with that caveat attached rather than quoted as current.

prices.note: HELD AT $356/mt FOB EAST AUSTRALIA (SMM-reported transaction of 30,000 mt for September loading dealt 05-Aug-2026, published 06-Aug). Eight runs without a public seaborne print is itself the finding, and it is reported rather than papered over. THE SUPPLY EVENT RESOLVED AND HAS STAYED RESOLVED FOR A SIXTH RUN. Norsk Hydro announced on 13-August that Alunorte in Barcarena, Para - 6.3 Mt/y nameplate and the largest alumina refinery outside China - is ramping back to FULL capacity after Brazil's regulator ANP approved it as a self-importer of natural gas and a temporary terminal-access agreement was reached with gas supplier CELBA. The disruption ran three days from the 11-August disclosure of a cut to 50%. Lost production is put at 100,000-120,000 tonnes with a guided potential Q3-2026 Bauxite & Alumina impact of US$75-100 million. THE HONEST READ IS UNCHANGED AND HARDENING: the cost consequence was never observed, because the outage never lasted long enough to produce a public seaborne price print and now almost certainly never will. Roughly 3 Mt/y annualised off the balance for three days is a rounding error against a 145 Mt/y global market. THE OTHER RECENT PRINT, STATED SEPARATELY BECAUSE THE BASIS DIFFERS AND MUST NOT BE BLENDED: SMM published on 11-August that 30,000 mt traded at $365/mt CIF MALAYSIA for September shipment, dealt 07-Aug-2026. CIF Malaysia is a delivered price including freight; FOB East Australia is a load-port price, so the $9/mt gap is broadly freight rather than a rally. MARGIN CONTEXT AT A LOWER METAL PRICE, AND IT MOVED THE WRONG WAY TODAY: against the 18-August three-month official of $3,234.00 the FOB mark now sits at about 11.0% of the metal price and the CIF mark at about 11.3%, both slightly HIGHER as ratios than yesterday purely because the metal fell $38.00 while the alumina marks did not move. Both remain well below the decade rule of thumb of roughly 15-17%, so the alumina leg is still a clear TAILWIND to smelter economics - but the direction of that ratio is now set by the metal price rather than by alumina, which is worth watching if the metal keeps falling.

prices.label: Bauxite (SMM imported index / Guinea CIF China)
prices.note: Carried at the 06-Aug-2026 SMM Bauxite Weekly Review. THE PUBLICATION RUNS ON A THURSDAY CADENCE AND THE NEXT EDITION IS DUE TOMORROW, 20-AUGUST; nothing newer had printed at this 03:35 London compile, so the row is carried rather than marked. SMM Imported Bauxite Index $71.57/mt, UP $0.70 week-on-week, Guinea CIF $70-74/mt (average +$1 w/w), Guinea FOB $38-42/mt (average +$1 w/w). CORROBORATION FROM THE 11-AUGUST COST REVIEW: imported bauxite prices 'sustained their upward trend in July, serving as the core driver behind the cost surge', citing elevated ocean freight and the Guinea rainy season reducing shipments, plus slow domestic Chinese mine resumption - to the point that 'some alumina producers have been forced to adjust production schedules'. SMM's forward view: 'no clear timeline has emerged for domestic supply recovery, while imported ore shipments are expected to shrink further amid the rainy season. Bauxite prices are likely to hold high and steady, with import quotes potentially edging slightly higher.' STRUCTURAL DEVELOPMENT CARRIED: Guinea's Mines Minister said state-owned Nimba Mining will sell bauxite to global traders and miners through MONTHLY TENDERS, with minimum guaranteed annual volumes under partner agreements and additional output sold via monthly spot tenders. Monthly tendering adds genuine public price discovery to the world's most important seaborne bauxite source and simultaneously shifts volume from contract to spot, which raises price variance in an already tight rainy-season market. THE NEXT SCHEDULED HARD DATAPOINT REMAINS THE GUINEA AUGUST LONG-TERM CONTRACT, still under negotiation against July's settlement of $70-71.5/mt. DRIVER DOWN, UNCHANGED: Chinese refinery bauxite inventories at roughly 94 days of cover. This remains the best-evidenced upward-trending input on the whole board, and it is the cost pressure that survives the Alunorte resolution entirely because it is about ore supply and freight rather than one refinery's gas contract.

items.note: SMM Fluoride Salt Weekly Review published 16-Aug-2026 via AL Circle: SMM mainstream aluminium fluoride quotations RMB 11,200-11,800/t, described as STABLE this week amid moderate trading sentiment. SMM describes the fluoride industry as caught in a negative loop of high costs, production losses and low operating rates, with most enterprises stepping up maintenance and flexible production cuts and prioritising long-term contract delivery, so incremental effective supply is limited. THE HARD NUMBER FOR A SMELTER COST LINE: the August aluminium fluoride TENDER PRICE of the benchmark aluminium enterprise was raised by RMB 250/t month-on-month, with upstream and downstream enterprises following suit. Smelters are reported to be purchasing cautiously, restocking only for rigid demand and pushing for lower prices. SMM expects a stable stalemate in the short term. For a metals board the relevance is generic rather than counterparty-specific: the Gulf accounted for roughly a tenth of global primary aluminium production before the conflict, and the corridor constraint is one of the two reasons that share is still impaired.

logistics.label: Red Sea / Bab al Mandeb corridor
logistics.note: Unchanged in substance and it should not be conflated with Hormuz. Most operators continue to route around the Cape of Good Hope, which adds roughly 10-14 days and the associated bunker and charter cost to Asia-Europe voyages. The 09-August strike on the Jazan refinery is a Red Sea littoral event rather than a Strait closure, and its relevance here is that it keeps war-risk pricing elevated across the whole basin rather than that it blocks any particular lane. logistics.label: Gulf war-risk insurance
logistics.note: War-risk cover for a VLCC transit is estimated at roughly 30 times pre-crisis levels on published market commentary. The mechanism that matters for a metals board is generic: war-risk premium is a per-voyage cost that lands on delivered prices regardless of who is shipping, so it inflates every regional premium that involves a Gulf leg without telling you anything about metal availability. It is a freight cost wearing a premium's clothing.

A 4% move in European gas on the same day the metal fell 1.6% is a margin squeeze from both ends for the European smelter fleet, and it is the second cost group after crude pointing upward this run.

headlines.title: THE FRONT END CROSSED INTO CONTANGO: cash $3,219.00 settled $15.00 BELOW the three-month of $3,234.00 on the 18-August official board, from exactly $0.00 on 17-August, a $2.00 backwardation on 14-August and $4.00 on 13-August. Four sessions of monotonic decay have carried the curve from a prompt premium to a prompt discount, the widest aluminium contango on the published board since 27-February. The market will not pay for prompt metal at a cycle-low inventory.

THE 34-SESSION DRAWDOWN STOPPED. LME aluminium warrant was UNCHANGED at 246,925 tonnes on 18-August, a reported daily change of exactly zero. SMM's independent flash note records the same pause at 246,900 mt, unchanged day on day, down 2.56% week on week and 11.84% month on month. The streak was the specific fact the tightness case cited; the longer-window decline is intact and that is stated alongside.

LME ALUMINIUM STOCKS OUTSIDE CHINA ARE 95 PER CENT RUSSIAN-ORIGIN, according to StoneX's senior metals analyst quoted by AL Circle - material US and European physical buyers are prohibited from using and many Asian buyers decline to purchase. The headline warrant number is therefore a weak proxy for Western-accessible metal in both directions. The same article describes aluminium as having 'returned to backwardation', a framing the 18-August board has already overtaken.

CHINA IS RELIEVING THE WESTERN SHORTAGE WITH SEMIS AND ALLOY RATHER THAN INGOT. Semi-finished exports hit 3.2 Mt in January-June, up 18% year on year, with June a record 695,000 t; alloy exports nearly doubled to 238,500 t and China became a net exporter of aluminium alloy in June for the first time since 2019. Primary exports rose 32% to 38,400 t, much of it likely re-exported bonded Western metal. Primary faces a 30% export tax; alloy and semis export at zero.

COPPER'S PROMPT PREMIUM COLLAPSED FROM $535.00 TO $255.00 as cash fell $515.00 and warrant BUILT 15,725 tonnes to 223,550 tonnes - the largest single-session inventory build on this board in the cycle. earnings.note: Revenue RMB 11.53bn, up 32.4% year on year. Net profit attributable to owners RMB 2.30bn, up 166.1%. EPS RMB 1.11 against RMB 0.58 in the corresponding period of last year, up 91.4%. THE CLEANEST PUBLIC READ THIS WEEK ON HOW FAR SMELTER MARGIN HAS EXPANDED AT 2026 PRICES, AND IT COMES FROM AN INTEGRATED, SELF-SUPPLIED PRODUCER. The company operates 788,100 t/y of electrolytic aluminium capacity in Huolinguole, Inner Mongolia with a captive power plant, plus an alumina refining and aluminium hydroxide base in Binzhou, Shandong; it states that self-sufficiency in alumina and electricity fully meets its production requirements. Profit attributable rose 166% on revenue up 32%, which is operating leverage of roughly five times and is only possible when the price rises against a cost base that does not. Management attributes the gain to higher electrolytic aluminium selling prices, lower production cost from a rising green-energy share, and an optimised financing structure. TWO FORWARD DISCLOSURES MATTER BEYOND the quarter: 1,040 MW of wind and 110 MW of solar were commissioned by end-June with the programme roughly 66% complete and the green share expected to exceed 50%, which lowers the cost base further; and the 500,000 t/y integrated electrolytic aluminium project in Saudi Arabia, invested with partners in 2025, had completed all compliance approvals with on-site construction in full swing. That project is a dated, sourced addition to the non-Chinese capacity pipeline. THE UNCOMFORTABLE IMPLICATION FOR PRICE BULLS: margins this wide at the low end of the cost curve are exactly the condition that funds new capacity, and this disclosure shows the funding and the capacity in the same document.

earnings.note: MARGINS EXPANDED SHARPLY WITH A THIRD OF THE VOLUME GONE. Adjusted net profit Dh2.46bn, up 34% year-on-year. Adjusted EBITDA Dh4.51bn, up 11% from Dh4.07bn, with the adjusted EBITDA margin widening to 33.3% from 27.0%. Revenue FELL 10% to Dh13.54bn from Dh15.08bn as aluminium sales dropped 32% to 939,000 t and cast metal production fell 29% to 1.01 Mt following the March incident at Al Taweelah. Reported net income Dh1.74bn after a Dh725m net incident impact. The company estimates around Dh1.5bn of capital expenditure to restore Al Taweelah, most of it in 2026, and guided hot metal back to pre-incident levels in Q1-2027 with the smelter currently at about 18% of capacity. THE COMPOSITION IS A PUBLIC CONFIRMATION OF THE MARGIN STRUCTURE THIS BOARD HAS DESCRIBED ALL CYCLE. Profit rose on three named drivers - higher realised aluminium prices, stronger regional premiums and LOWER ALUMINA PRICES - while a third of the sales volume was simply unavailable. A 630 basis-point margin expansion on a 10% revenue decline is only possible when the cost side has fallen faster than the top line, and the alumina leg is the reason. IT ALSO EXPLAINS TODAY'S PRICE ACTION IN ONE LINE: the same release that showed the margin also showed the recovery date, and the market traded the recovery date. The read-across to the alumina panel is direct - if Alunorte's 50% rate ends up lifting seaborne alumina, this is the margin that compresses first across the Gulf fleet.

The EBITDA margin printed 16.42% against 12.31% in Q1 FY26 and 12.82% in Q4 FY26 - a 411 basis-point expansion year-on-year and 360 basis points sequentially. INDIA ALUMINIUM UPSTREAM delivered its highest-ever quarterly EBITDA at RS 7,390cr, up 81%, comfortably exceeding the prior record of RS 5,448cr set in Q4 FY26. The COPPER segment also set a record at RS 918cr, up 36%. NOVELIS, the downstream subsidiary, reported adjusted EBITDA of $516m, up 24% from $416m a year earlier and equivalent to RS 4,875cr (+37%), with net income of $164m (+71%) and adjusted EBITDA of roughly $563 per tonne, helped by the restart of the Oswego hot mill in early June 2026 and continued Bay Minette commissioning. THIS IS THE CLEANEST PUBLIC EVIDENCE AVAILABLE OF HOW AN INTEGRATED PRODUCER CONVERTS THE 2026 PRICE STRUCTURE INTO MARGIN, AND THE CONVERSION RATE IS VERY HIGH. Revenue rose 32% while EBITDA rose 73% and upstream aluminium EBITDA rose 81% - operating leverage of well over two times on the upstream leg. The mechanism is integration: captive bauxite, captive alumina and captive coal-fired power insulate the cost stack from exactly the two legs that are currently rising for non-integrated smelters, namely seaborne bauxite (SMM index $71.57/mt, +$0.70 w/w) and seaborne alumina ($356/mt FOB East Australia on the 05-Aug trade). THE CONTRAST WITH CENTURY IS THE POINT. Century Aluminum, which buys its alumina, has now cited unfavourable raw-material price realisation as its principal EBITDA headwind for two consecutive quarters; Hindalco, which makes its own, posted a record. Management had guided to roughly 5% sequential aluminium cost inflation into this quarter and still delivered a record, which says the LME move more than absorbed it. FOR THE MARKET VIEW: this is bullish for the margin narrative and neutral-to-bearish for the supply narrative, because producers earning at this level have every incentive to run flat out and to accelerate the restart pipeline.

earnings.note: Q2-2026 profit attributable to equity holders BHD 64.9m (US$172.5m), +164% y/y; Q2 EBITDA US$295m; EPS 46 fils. H1 profit BHD 140.2m (US$372.8m), +228% y/y; EPS 99 fils. OPERATIONALLY THE WEAKEST PRINT IN THE PEER SET: Q2 net finished production 155,469 t, DOWN 61% y/y, and sales volume 280,799 t, -32% y/y, with Lines 1, 2 and 3 still under controlled shutdown on regional tensions and raw-material availability. Value-added product was 195,891 t, 70% of shipments. THE SHARPEST ILLUSTRATION ON THIS BOARD OF WHAT THE 2026 MARKET IS ACTUALLY REWARDING: a producer can lose 61% of its output year-on-year and still nearly triple half-year profit, because average LME rose 46% y/y to $3,576/t in Q2. It also quantifies the supply loss the deficit rests on - Alba's own read put the Q2 global deficit at 934,000 t including China and 626,000 t excluding it, with global supply contracting about 1% mainly on Middle East disruption. Management explicitly framed the curtailments as preserving flexibility for a swift recovery when conditions improve, which is the restart option the bearish case depends on. Separately Alba is progressing its US$2.2bn acquisition of Aluminium Dunkerque, about 300,000 t/y and the largest EU smelter.

status.name: Rio Tinto (RIO) / Tomago
status.status: TOMAGO SECURED - A$2.5bn GOVERNMENT SUPPORT, POWER CONTRACTED TO 2038, A$1.1bn INVESTMENT
status.impact: A CLOSURE RISK OVER UP TO 590,000 t/y - ALMOST 40% OF AUSTRALIAN PRODUCTION - HAS BEEN REMOVED. Tomago will enter a ten-year power purchase agreement after its existing contract expires on 31-Dec-2028, taking supply to 2038 and to fully renewable electricity from 2033, and will invest A$1.1bn in real terms through 2038 including A$100m for decarbonisation, cutting Scope 1 and 2 emissions by 7.1 Mt/y from 2033. Bearish for price, structurally significant for the western smelter fleet - and the fact that a smelter this size needed public support to contract power is the most honest public statement available about western smelter economics.

status.name: China operators (aggregate)
status.status: At the 45 Mt policy ceiling; H1 primary production +2.2% while Citi's end-use tracker fell 0.4% y/y - the surplus is being exported as semis and alloy rather than ingot
status.impact: REFRESHED ON THE 16-AUGUST SMM WEEKLY. China's weekly aluminium production was basically stable over the past week and the proportion of liquid aluminium rose 0.11 percentage point week-on-week - a marginal shift toward direct-to-casthouse delivery rather than ingot. Effectively no headroom remains for further Chinese supply growth against the 45 Mt policy ceiling, so the growth is being exported to Indonesia and elsewhere instead. On the demand side the same review places the downstream processing industry in its traditional consumption off-season with operating rates under pressure, and flags that aluminium billet processing fees pulled back, weakening replacement demand for aluminium ingot - the mechanism that could slow the destocking SMM itself expects to continue but decelerate in the second half of the month.
status.update: REFRESHED ON AL CIRCLE'S 18-AUGUST TRADE ANALYSIS AND THE NEW DETAIL IS THE MOST IMPORTANT ADDITION TO THIS PANEL THIS WEEK. China's primary aluminium production rose 2.2% in the first half with smelters operating close to or slightly above the 45 Mt policy cap, while Citi's China end-use demand tracker FELL 0.4% year on year on weakness in traditional sectors, particularly construction. A production increase against a demand decrease produces exportable surplus, and the export data shows exactly where it went: semi-finished exports of 3.2 million tonnes in January-June, up 18% year on year, with June at a record 695,000 tonnes; alloy exports nearly doubling to 238,500 tonnes with China turning NET EXPORTER of aluminium alloy in June for the first time since 2019; and primary exports up 32% to 38,400 tonnes, much of which the article attributes to Western-origin metal held in Chinese bonded warehouses being redirected rather than to Chinese production leaving. THE TAX STRUCTURE IS THE MECHANISM AND IT IS PUBLIC: primary aluminium exports face a 30% tax while alloy and semis export at a zero rate, so the surplus leaves in processed form. SHFE inventories were put at 422,097 tonnes against LME inventory of 358,000 tonnes including off-warrant stocks. On the demand side, SMM's 18-August scrap review describes cast aluminium alloy operating rates continuing to decline through the high-temperature holidays and the consumption off-season with order volumes shrinking.

trade.note: TRADE CORRIDORS ARE REVIEWED MONTHLY OR ON MATERIAL CHANGE AND ARE DELIBERATELY NOT CHURNED DAILY. THIS RUN CARRIES A GENUINE MATERIAL CHANGE AND THE PANEL IS UPDATED ACCORDINGLY, WHICH IS WHY THE AS-OF DATE MOVED. AL Circle published a detailed analysis on 18-August quantifying how China is filling the Western supply gap created by the Gulf losses, and the composition of that flow is a corridor fact rather than a price fact: semi-finished aluminium exports of 3.2 million tonnes in January-June, up 18% year on year, with June shipments of 695,000 tonnes a monthly record; alloy exports nearly doubling to 238,500 tonnes, with China becoming a NET EXPORTER of aluminium alloy in June for the first time since 2019; and primary exports up 32% to 38,400 tonnes, much of which is attributed to Western-origin metal held in Chinese bonded warehouses being redirected rather than to Chinese production leaving the country - Chinese data recorded 9,700 tonnes exported to the United States in January-June against US customs data recording only 70 tonnes of Chinese imports. The tax structure is the mechanism: primary aluminium exports face a 30% tax while alloy and semis export at a zero rate, and Beijing removed the 13% VAT export rebate on aluminium products in December 2024, which cut semis exports 18% to 890,000 tonnes last year before the Gulf disruption revived them. THE SECOND-ORDER CONSEQUENCE IS EXPLICITLY FLAGGED IN THE SOURCE AND BELONGS ON A TRADE PANEL: when Western buyers import Chinese bars, rods and tubes instead of raw metal for local conversion, fabrication activity relocates, which is why Western policymakers have imposed anti-dumping duties on Chinese aluminium products. THE REST OF THE CORRIDOR PICTURE IS UNCHANGED AND WAS RE-VERIFIED: the Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed on day 171 with no development dated after the 16-August restatement, and Trading Economics headlines both crude benchmarks as extending gains on the US-Iran stalemate; Red Sea routing around the Cape of Good Hope continues, adding roughly 10-14 days to Asia-Europe voyages; and Section 232 was re-verified this run at 50% on aluminium articles and 25% on derivatives, with the US-content relief threshold cut from 95% to 85% in June-2026 and Annex I-C carve-outs at 15% for Japan, Korea, the UK, Switzerland, Taiwan and the EU.

catalysts.text: TODAY'S LME OFFICIAL, AND THE TEST IS NOW BINARY AND CHEAP TO SCORE. THE QUESTION IS WHETHER THE CONTANGO IS ONE SESSION OR A REGIME. The cash-3M spread crossed from exactly $0.00 to a $15.00 CONTANGO on 18-August, the widest prompt discount on the published board since 27-February. A return to a flat or backwardated spread today would mark 18-August as a one-day artefact of what was unmistakably a complex-wide repricing - four of the five metals loosened their front ends and copper's premium halved on the largest single-day stock build of the cycle. A SECOND CONSECUTIVE CONTANGO, or an outright stock BUILD after yesterday's flat print, would confirm that the seven-week drawdown was never about prompt scarcity and would be the most bearish structural sequence this board has produced. SECOND, THE LEVELS. The wave (iv) low at $3,229.50 broke on cash by $10.50 and held on the three-month by $4.50; the count has been relabelled rather than defended. The new explicit invalidation is the 28-July swing low at $3,159.50, now $59.50 below cash - a close beneath it takes the correction deeper than a simple second wave allows and opens $3,105 and then $3,061.50. On the upside $3,254.60 is the 38.2% retracement of the whole $3,061.50-to-$3,374.00 advance and is the first level bulls need back.

THE CHINESE EXCHANGE INVENTORY SERIES IS THE ONE THAT HAS NOT PAUSED, AND IT IS THE SINGLE MOST USEFUL DAILY CHECK LEFT FOR THE BULL CASE. SHFE aluminium futures warrants were recorded at 292,929 mt on 18-August, down 2,916 mt on the day, down 11,262 mt (3.70%) over the past week and down 86,862 mt (22.87%) over the past month - roughly double the LME's own 11.84% monthly rate of decline. If that series also decelerates or turns while the LME stays flat, the last independent inventory support for the tightness case is gone. If it keeps running at this rate while the LME is flat, the divergence between the two exchanges becomes the story, and the reported 95% Russian-origin share of ex-China LME warrant becomes the obvious explanation for it.

SMM BAUXITE WEEKLY REVIEW - DUE TOMORROW ON THE PUBLICATION'S THURSDAY CADENCE. The last edition carried here (06-August) had the SMM Imported Bauxite Index at $71.57/mt, up $0.70 week on week, with Guinea CIF at $70-74/mt and Guinea FOB at $38-42/mt. Bauxite is the identified core driver of the rise in Chinese alumina full production cost and remains the best-evidenced upward-trending input on this board - the structural cost pressure that survives the Alunorte resolution entirely, because it is about ore supply and freight rather than one refinery's gas contract. The August Guinea long-term contract remains under negotiation against July's $70-71.5/mt settlement, and Guinea's move to monthly spot tenders through a state-owned vehicle adds public price discovery while shifting volume from contract to spot.

MJP Q4-2026 PREMIUM NEGOTIATIONS conventionally open against the Q3-2026 settlement of $395/t CIF Japan. A dedicated search this run again returned nothing dated after the 06-July settlement - no producer offers, no negotiation levels, no settlement coverage - so the pending quarter remains a SCENARIO RANGE of $305-395 and NOT an assessment. THE RANGE IS HELD UNCHANGED BUT THE BALANCE INSIDE IT MOVED FURTHER TOWARD BUYERS ON 18-AUGUST, AND THIS TIME THE MECHANISM IS ARITHMETIC RATHER THAN ATMOSPHERIC: a seller's strongest argument in a premium negotiation is a backwardated front end, and that argument has not merely gone - it has INVERTED into a $15.00 prompt discount on the exchange's own settlement. Buyers additionally gained a paused LME drawdown and a public statement that ex-China LME stock is 95% Russian-origin material Western buyers cannot use. Sellers retain a cycle-low inventory, a closed Strait, a second consecutive quarterly decline in ex-China refined production, and an 18%-restarted Gulf smelter. PROLONGED HORMUZ CLOSURE KEEPS GULF SUPPLY IMPAIRED. Day 171 counted to today's report date. AN ALUMINA COST SHOCK RE-EMERGES. TREND DOWN. The Alunorte gas disruption - the only credible alumina cost threat of the year - resolved in three days via ANP self-import approval and a temporary CELBA terminal-access agreement, with lost production of 100,000-120,000 t against a roughly 145 Mt/y global market and no public seaborne price print produced at any point. Against a decade rule of thumb of 15-17% alumina remains a clear tailwind, but the ratio now moves with the metal. THE RESIDUAL RISK IS THE WORD 'TEMPORARY' IN THE CELBA AGREEMENT, and the longer-run risk is upstream of the refinery - the thread running through the Guinea contract negotiations, elevated ocean freight and the rainy season.

SMELTER ENERGY AND CARBON COSTS RE-INFLATE - AND THE AUGUST SETTLEMENT WINDOW HAS NOW CLOSED WITH NOTHING PUBLISHED. Refined production outside China has now fallen year-on-year for a SECOND consecutive quarter on StoneX's public statement, driven by the Gulf smelter's 61% second-quarter decline and the Alunorte interruption. A PRIMARY DEFICIT AND A COMFORTABLE SEMI-FINISHED MARKET ARE NOT CONTRADICTORY - they are what you get when the surplus of a capped producer leaves in fabricated form.
